text:
Bronchial breathing is loud, harsh, high-pitched breath sounds in which expiration is louder and longer than inspiration, with a pause between the two phases. It is normally heard only over the trachea and large airways, so hearing it over the lung periphery suggests consolidation, such as pneumonia. The team note reverses the phases; the expiratory phase is the louder, longer one, and the pause falls between inspiration and expiration.

CONFIDENCE: 90
